subject: PatientPortal: sudden token culling and degraded throughput impacting peak workflows
messages:
From: Jane Lee <j.lee@veridianhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@veridianhealth.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: PatientPortal — morning peak: 429s + slow responses

Marissa,

We started seeing a spike in 429s and token-related latency on the PatientPortal this morning around 08:45 PST. Our clinicians reported slow search/autocomplete and some of the high-frequency workflows timed out. I attached a screenshot of the token/throughput graph and a zipped set of request logs (veridian_logs_20261120.zip).

Key observations from our side:
- Errors: ~4–6% 429s across the 08:45–09:10 window.
- Latency: median API response time jumped from ~85ms to ~450ms.
- Pattern: bursty traffic from imports and peak UI autosaves — looks like short bursts of very high token rates.

Can you confirm if any rate-limit / quota / burst policy changes were deployed this morning? This is impacting patient workflows; we need immediate mitigation and an explanation so we can brief our leadership and procurement.

Thanks,
Jane Lee
Director of Engineering
Veridian Health

Attachments: screenshot_rate_graph.png, veridian_logs_20261120.zip

Short answer: we did not roll a global rate-limit change this morning on your account. That said, I've looped in Karthik (AE) and Monica (CS) to coordinate with Ops. Connor (infra) will triage whether a burst-window or quota fence caused the rapid request culling.

- Jane: please share any additional traces for the 08:30–09:30 window if available. The attached logs were helpful.

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: PatientPortal — morning peak: 429s + slow responses

Quick triage notes (summary of infra findings):
- Observed symptom: Veridian's tenant rapidly exhausted their burst_credit pool between 08:42:30 and 08:49:10 due to several short, very high-QPS bursts (imports + autosave sync).
- Root cause signal: The customer's burst_window was configured conservatively (burst_window=60s, burst_credits set to a low value for the Dedicated pool tier). When the window arithmetic ran, requests were culled aggressively (token culling + short-term deny).
- No global policy change or control-plane rollout executed this morning. This was a misalignment between the customer's traffic pattern and the policy parameters on their Dedicated reservation.

Immediate remedial actions executed at 10:50 PST:
1) Temporary override: increased burst_credits by 4x for VHD-3471 and extended burst_window to 180s to avoid rapid credit exhaustion.
2) Applied a short-lived emergency rule to accept legacy token share semantics for the next 3 hours.
3) Opened INF-1122 to track a permanent fix and triage.

Next steps / remediation plan:
- Short-term (today): monitor the tenant for 2 full peak cycles; if stable, we will keep the emergency rule until a config update is ready. (Action: Connor)
- Medium-term (48–72h): product to propose safer default burst calculus for Dedicated customers with bursty desktop clients. (Action: Neha)
- Post-mortem (within 5 business days): internal RCA + customer-facing summary and configuration recommendations. (Action: Marissa / Monica)

Attachments: extracted_burst_metrics_20261120.csv (summary)

Connor O'Brien
Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com

Jane — following up with a customer-facing summary and next steps after today's mitigation work. Apologies again for the disruption this morning; appreciate your patience while we stabilized the environment.

What we found:
- The immediate impact was caused by rapid depletion of tenant burst credits under a 60s burst_window; as a result, short high-QPS bursts were being denied leading to elevated 429s and higher tail latency.

What we did (today):
- Temporary mitigation at 10:50 PST: 4x burst_credits increase + burst_window extended to 180s.
- Emergency rule applied to accept older token-sharing semantics for 3 hours to smooth request acceptance.

Planned actions:
- We will implement a safe default change for Dedicated pool burst calculus to better tolerate short high-frequency client bursts. (ETA: during next weekly release; Neha leading)
- Connor will monitor metrics for two peak cycles and confirm stabilization; we'll share a monitoring dashboard link within 2 hours.
- Post-mortem and a configuration recommendation doc (how to tune burst_window and credits for clinical workloads) will be delivered within 5 business days.

Immediate asks for Veridian:
- Can you confirm whether you ran any large import or scheduled burst jobs in the morning? We saw signs of parallel imports from several IPs in the logs.
- If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute technical huddle tomorrow to walk through recommended settings and avoid recurrence.

If agreeable, Karthik and Monica will coordinate a credit/contract amendment (short-term) and follow up on pricing/commit changes if you want a long-term higher baseline.

Thanks — will be standing by until you confirm the stabilizing metrics.

—Marissa
